Progression

Material Realms and relics

What a swing in each Material Realm pays at every promotion, which fight unlocks each realm level, and what every relic level costs — the normal ladder and each season's ladder, which differ at the same level.

Material Realms

The game's own rule card: "Use specific items in mines/caves to gather ores and defeat monsters for rewards." "The rankings will track the number of ores mined and monsters defeated." "Rankings data resets every Monday at the reset time." Each realm keeps one object in front of you at a time. A swing spends one tool and takes a bite of the object's durability; every point of durability you remove pays the object's per-point reward, and breaking it pays the break reward on top. The next object is drawn from the realm's pool. Quick mode swings until the object breaks (64 swings at most per request) and unlocks once Loong Haven is open; the realm itself unlocks when you clear its first unlock fight, and the entry shows from Apprentice I. There are no free daily swings in this build.

The swing

Damage per swing is the realm's attack times a roll between 0.9 and 1.1, times 1.5 on a crit, rounded to the nearest point (GetMopUpDamage). The stats come from level_prop and are the same at every character level: 10 damage, 20% crit for ×1.5, about 11.0 durability per swing on average, identical in all four realms. So a 90-durability node takes about 9 swings, and the number that grows with your promotion is not the damage but what each point of durability pays.

What each object pays

At the No Rank factor of 1. Every count except Refined Ore and Dawnium is multiplied by the promotion factor below and rounded down at each step (their reward rows use the constant column, so they stay flat). The first objects a fresh realm shows are fixed: Ironvein Pit: Raw Ore Mine, Raw Ore Mine, Refined Ore Mine, Raw Ore Mine, Raw Ore Mine; Gilded Depths: Rolla Mine, Rolla Mine, Dawnium Mine, Rolla Mine, Rolla Mine; Dread Hollow: Gnoll Bruiser, Gnoll Archor, Gnoll Rider, Gnoll Shielder, Gnoll Sentinel; Dustfall Dune: Chrono Sand Mine, Chrono Sand Mine, Moment Sand Mine, Chrono Sand Mine, Chrono Sand Mine. Abandoned chests cost no tool, break at once and do not count for the weekly ranking.

Yield by promotion

The count of every scaled reward is the base count times level_number column 6 at your promotion's position in the SubRank list, rounded down (RewardRuleInfoParser). The client sends the swing and the server rolls the reward; the sub-rank it reads is your own, which is how the yield rises the day you promote. The cells give the common node of each realm, broken in full; the percentage is the rise over the tier before. Other objects scale the same way: multiply their base counts above by the factor.

Unlocking each realm level

Each level opens when you clear the corresponding fight on the world map ("Clear the fight in its region to unlock"). The fights are ordinary stages with a first-clear reward (stage.Awards), scaled by the stage's own tier rather than yours (AwardUsePlayerLevelAndSubRank is off).

Relic levels

Relics have one ladder of normal levels, capped by your promotion (system_level_limit: the cap rises by one per tier), and above the cap the level you see is a season level, as the game puts it: "Levels beyond your Rank's cap are calculated as Season Levels." A season level is only for sale at the top tier of the season's promotion, its cost comes from the season's ladder (treasure_bless, keyed by your promotion family), and when the season ends "Season Levels will expire and convert" to the Astral Pact currency. So the same number costs different things in different seasons. Level 10 → 11, for instance: in Season 1 it is season level 1, sold at Expert III only: 3,200 Rare Chrono Sand and 28,800 Rolla; from Season 2 to 5 it is normal level 11, open from Champion I: 900 Epic Chrono Sand and 40,500 Rolla.

Where this comes from. Realms: mop_up_dungeon (tools, unlock fights, object pools), mop_up_material (durability, per-point and break reward rules), reward_rule scaled by level_number as RewardRuleInfoParser.GetRewardDropInfosByRuleList does it, level_prop for the swing stats, BattleFormulaHandler.GetMopUpDamage for the roll, game_settings.MopUp, rule_tip for the card text, stage and stage_map_location for the unlock fights. Relics: treasure_levelup_material, treasure_bless, treasure_upgrade_material, system_level_limit and system_level_gap_limit, read the way TreasureHelper.GetTreasureLevelUpCostMaterials and CheckLevelLimits read them; seasons from astrological_season_config. Names are the game's English strings. One assumption: the server pays the per-point reward per point of durability removed; the client never computes it, so a swing that overkills an object may pay for the whole roll or only for the durability left.

Purrwikimania — an independent, fan-made reference for Sword x Staff (Boltray Games). Every number here is read directly out of the game's own configuration files and decompiled code, not from testing or estimation. Item names are the game's official English strings.
